## Circular to All Licensed Corporations

## Reminder to comply with certain Code and Internal Control Guidelines requirements

The Commission wishes to remind all licensed corporations of their duties under the General Principles  set  out  in  the  Code  of  Conduct  for  Persons  Licensed  by  or  Registered  with  the Securities  and  Futures  Commission  (Code).    Licensed  corporations  should  abide  by  these General Principles, which are fundamental to the undertaking of their businesses.

The General Principles reinforce core values such as acting in the best interests of clients; acting  with  due  skill,  care  and  diligence;  having  resources  and  procedures  required  for  the proper performance of their business activities; seeking and providing appropriate necessary information from and to clients; avoiding conflicts of interest; complying with all applicable regulatory  requirements  and  safeguarding  client  assets.    The  Commission  expects  senior management  to  bear  primary  responsibility  for  ensuring  the  maintenance  of  appropriate standards of conduct and adherence to proper procedures by the firm.

In  particular,  the  Commission  wishes  to  draw  attention  to  certain  fundamental  regulatory requirements  set  out  in  the  Code  and  the  Management,  Supervision  and  Internal  Control Guidelines for Person Licensed by or Registered with the Securities and Futures Commission.

## I. Know Your Client

- A  licensed  corporation  should  take  all  reasonable  steps  to  establish  the  financial situation,  investment  experience  and  investment  objectives  of  each  of  its  clients relevant to the services to be provided.
- A  licensed  corporation  should  assure  itself  that  the  client  who  trades  in  derivative products  (such  as  options,  derivative  warrants  or  leveraged  financial  products) understands the nature and risk of the products and has sufficient net worth to be able to assume the risks and bear the potential loss resulting from such trading.

In this connection, a licensed corporation should ensure that its staff members are fit and proper and otherwise qualified to explain the nature and risk of such products to its clients (including having relevant training or experience).

## II. Prudent Risk Management

- A licensed corporation should be vigilant in monitoring its business risks, including credit, market and liquidity risk, and at all times exercise prudent risk management. In particular, it should:
- ¾ monitor and keep its risk exposure firmly under control, including  intra-day and overnight exposures arising from its business;
- ¾ ensure  that  the  financial  status  of  clients  is  commensurate  with  the  risks arising from the client's transactions;
- ¾ avoid  building  up  excessive  or  over  concentrated  exposures  in  individual counterparties, products or markets;
- ¾ mitigate uncovered market or credit exposures through consistent and timely implementation of established risk management measures such as margining requirements; and
- ¾ determine the effect of abnormal and significant changes in market conditions on the firm using various quantitative and qualitative variable assumptions,

so  as  to  ensure  that  the  firm  has  adequate  capital  and  liquidity  for  the  business undertaken by the firm.

## III. Management Responsibilities

- The senior management should ensure that
- ¾ reporting lines are clearly identified;
- ¾ supervisory  and  reporting  responsibilities  are  assigned  to  appropriate  staff members;
- ¾ detailed policies and procedures pertaining to authorizations and approvals are clearly defined and communicated and followed by staff; and
- ¾ management and supervisory functions should be performed by qualified and experienced individuals only.
